world_org_meetings.title: UNGA 81: Five key takeaways from general debate
world_org_meetings.description: The 81st United Nations General Assembly ends with AI, Palestine and wars dominating speeches.

world_org_meetings.title: In UN address, Anand takes jab at 'great powers' disrupting global order
world_org_meetings.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand has put "strategic autonomy" at the forefront of Canada's address to the United Nations General Assembly today.

world_org_meetings.title: Former U.S. Ambassador to Israel on Netanyahu's speech at UNGA
world_org_meetings.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with former U.S. Ambassador to Israel Thomas Nides about Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's speech at the United Nations General Assembly.

world_org_meetings.title: Pope in Paris, Xi in DC, AI at a Crossroads
world_org_meetings.description: It’s been a week of walkouts, power plays and diplomatic theatre — from a battle over press freedom in Washington, to a United Nations General Assembly marked by protests and departures, as leaders clashed over Iran, Cuba and Venezuela. There was also a rare red-carpet meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, as the US and China extended their trade truce and turned their attention to the race for dominance in artificial intelligence. And from the geopolitical to the spiritual, Pope Leo brought his call for restraint and regulation of AI to France, as he sought to position the Vatican as a moral voice in a rapidly changing world.

world_org_meetings.title: Actors Susan Sarandon, Hannah Einbinder among detained protesters outside Netanyahu's UN speech
world_org_meetings.description: Actors Susan Sarandon and Hannah Einbinder were among the protestors detained in New York City on Thursday as Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu delivered a speech to the United Nations General Assembly.

diplomatic_visits.title: Spanish royals welcome French President Macron in official ceremony
diplomatic_visits.description: Spain's King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia welcomed French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte Macron during an official ceremony upon their arrival at Madrid's Royal Palace. French President Macron is on a two-day official visit in Spain. This state visit will serve to highlight and strengthen the ties and bilateral relations between the two countries. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid, Spain.

diplomatic_visits.title: UAE confirms president met with Israel's PM Netanyahu in Abu Dhabi on Sunday
diplomatic_visits.description: The visit came weeks after a bombshell Israeli media report that the Emirati president had warned Netanyahu ahead of the Hamas-led attack on Israel in 2023, which the Israeli premier did not pass on to the security services.

diplomatic_visits.title: Trump offered to sell arms to China during Xi visit, US ambassador tells Fox News
diplomatic_visits.description: The United States is required by law to supply Taiwan, which has a democratically elected president and legislature, with weapons for its defence under the 1979 Taiwan Relations Act.

diplomatic_visits.title: REPLAY: France's Macron speaks on European Union as pope visits Metz
diplomatic_visits.description: French President Emmanuel Macron said that Europe must rediscover the “courage of its founders” and not give in to the “resurgence of nationalism" as he delivered an address alongside Pope Leo XIV in Metz on the last day of the pontiff's visit to France.

diplomatic_visits.title: Trump gave Xi Jinping a warm welcome. What did the talks accomplish?
diplomatic_visits.description: From the National Archives to the state dinner, President Trump and Xi Jinping looked comfortable together in Washington. Two former NPR China correspondents on what the visit did and didn't deliver.

elections.title: Trump trade adviser says Canada will 'pay even more dearly' if 'you interfere' in U.S. midterms
elections.description: One of U.S. President Donald Trump's trade advisers is threatening repercussions for Canada if it "interferes" in the upcoming midterm elections — though it's not clear what he anticipates the country would do to impact the vote.

elections.title: A view from Brazil: The fight for the favela vote
elections.description: In Brazil, more than 158 million voters are being called to the polls on Sunday to elect their next president, as well as new members of Congress and governors. In Rio de Janeiro, local candidates are fighting for one particularly sought-after electorate: the residents of favelas. FRANCE 24’s Jan Onoszko reports from Rocinha, Brazil’s largest favela.

elections.title: French far-right leader Bardella denies anti-Semitism accusations
elections.description: 🇫🇷 ✡️ Far-right #NationalRally (RN) party leader Jordan #Bardella has denied accusation by French investigative website #Mediapart that he made anti-Semitic comments on private chats in 2013. It comes as RN candidate Marine #LePen is polling well in the lead for the 2027 presidential election.

elections.title: France's Le Pen defiant after top ally hit by antisemitism claims
elections.description: French far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen on Tuesday vowed to hit back at allegations of antisemitism targeting her de-facto number two Jordan Bardella, which have punctured her buoyant campaign at a time she is riding high in the polls. Le Pen, who is aiming to win the Elysee at her fourth attempt next year in a far-right breakthrough that would send a shockwave across Europe, lambasted the Mediapart website that published the claims and said Bardella has her "total confidence".

elections.title: Brazil's countdown to election day: Crime and security high on voters' agenda
elections.description: Security is a central issue in Brazil’s presidential campaign, in a country where gangs and militias have tightened their grip in recent years. Lula is accused of losing ground amid rising insecurity and violence — an issue seized on by Flavio Bolsonaro and the far right. Rio de Janeiro is one of the country’s most violent cities and a showcase for public security policy. How are Rio residents experiencing this insecurity, and will it influence their vote? FRANCE 24's Fanny Lothaire and Jan Onoszko report.
